trending.title: How we ran the Kiro University Challenge as a community build-along: 141 builders at AWS User Group Madurai
trending.description: A community case study and playbook from AWS User Group Madurai. We - Vivek, Logesh and Poobalan turned Kiro's seven-lesson University Challenge into a build-along with four evening Circle sessions, a one-command setup that created a compliant repo and progress tracking, a leaderboard ranked by active days, and community rewards earned by rank. 141 members joined, 77 linked a repo, 38 demonstrated all seven lessons. Includes the numbers, what went wrong, and how to run it without a custom platform.

trending.title: Enterprise-Grade AI Agent Architecture Analysis on AWS: The Synergy of Amazon Bedrock and MCP
trending.description:
After attending AWS Cloud Day in Vietnam, I want to record the valuable insights I gained at the event.

The evolution of Generative AI is rapidly shifting from standalone Large Language Models (LLMs) to autonomous AI Agents capable of reasoning, acting, and interacting directly with enterprise data. This architecture outlines a comprehensive and robust solution on the AWS platform, maximizing the Amazon Bedrock ecosystem in conjunction with the MCP (Model Context Protocol) communication standard.

trending.title: Benchmarking Strands Decider, LLM Classifiers and Bedrock Routing for Model Routing
trending.description: I routed 216 graded requests across Amazon Nova and Claude models with Strands Decider, five LLM classifiers, Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing and Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization. The decider judged request difficulty perfectly (ROC AUC 1.00 against 0.88 for Claude Sonnet 4.6) but cost about 0.0012 USD and 11 to 13 s per decision on a CPU microVM. Here are the numbers and the rules I now follow for when a decision model should judge and when a small LLM should route.

trending.title: Strands Box on AWS Lambda MicroVMs: a kernel per agent, a policy per command, and a fleet to run them with microvm-ctl
trending.description: Strands Box checks every shell command, file and request an agent makes against a Dogwood policy. Lambda MicroVMs give the agent its own kernel. I built Box for aarch64 Linux, ran it inside Lambda MicroVMs, and drove fleets with microvm-ctl: 83 ms per box, 22.7 boxes/s per 1 GB VM, 64 of 64 correct across 8 VMs, a playground app, and the bugs I hit.
